More and more I am coming to accept that our understanding of the sciences were but limited by our desire to have solutions that we could understand.

We’re not aware of any law firm going to this extreme.

For example Latham is buying GPUs but is also firm-wide on Harvey and we announced a deeper partnership today.

We think that’s the right strategy and what matters more than build vs buy is how heavily a firm is investing in AI.

The best way to invest is a portfolio approach of working closely with vertical vendors and the labs and cloud providers while also self-building with open source and the frontier ecosystem.

Everything is moving too fast and law firms are too complex for a single binary approach like this post suggests.

Law firms will not rely on a single vendor nor will they build the entire stack themselves.

My view is that longer term the labs and clouds will build general intelligence infrastructure and vertical players will help customize it for each industry.

Then individual firms will leverage their unique data, human expertise and workflows to build differentiated AI to better compete against their peers and serve their clients.

Our goal is to build the trusted vertical layer and open it up through APIs so firms can build everything from custom models and context layers to agents and products with us.

And most importantly do it in a way they can trust that their data and their clients’ data is safe and only used for their benefit.
